subject: Private Offer - TerraFirm (Azure): list-price anchoring, channel margin & invoice routing
messages:
From: Sara Hayden <sara.hayden@terrafirm.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private Offer draft + ask on listing and partner margin

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the draft PO. We reviewed the numbers this morning - overall looks promising but procurement needs clarity on two items before we can move to signature:

1) List-price anchoring in Marketplace: the draft uses a list price that is materially higher than what our reseller (CloudBridge) expects. They require evidence that the list price isn't just a vehicle for an inflated discount. Please confirm the rationale and provide any marketplace listing comparables.

2) Channel margin pass-through: CloudBridge needs at least a 20% net margin on resold Reserved Nodes. Your draft appears to assume a 12% broker fee. Can Redwood either (a) increase the private-offer discount to preserve partner margin, or (b) commit to invoicing the distributor differently so they can claim an acceptable margin?

We also need a clear invoice routing model - whether Redwood will invoice TerraFirm directly or CloudBridge will invoice customers and Redwood will invoice CloudBridge. That impacts our procurement approvals.

Can your team respond with a short proposal and an updated PO by Monday 6/1? I can loop in our channel lead if needed.

Regards,
Sara
Procurement Manager | TerraFirm

Attachments: TF-procurement-rules.pdf (reference)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hayden <sara.hayden@terrafirm.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer draft + ask on listing and partner margin

Hi Sara - thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then next steps:

- List-price anchoring: the list price in the draft is based on our reserved-node MSRP for enterprise SKUs; we can provide a short comparables pack. We avoid lowering list price because it reduces visibility into discount economics for internal billing and marketplace analytics. That said, we can add an auditor-facing note on the listing to explain this private-offer promotion.

- Channel margin: we get CloudBridge's position. Two rapid options:
  Option A) Increase the headline private-offer discount by 6 percentage points on the Reserved Node line so the partner recovers margin; OR
  Option B) Keep the headline discount but change invoice routing so Redwood invoices CloudBridge net of reseller commission (CloudBridge then invoices TerraFirm). Option B preserves list-price reporting while enabling partner economics.

- Invoice routing: we recommend Option B if procurement and CloudBridge prefer a clean reseller margin line. I'll attach an invoice-routing diagram and a sample invoice template for review.

I'll circulate an updated PO with both options Monday morning (6/1) and include comparables for marketplace listings. CCing Ben for channel impact and Laura for revenue recognition / finance ops checks.

Best,
Jordan
Head of Marketplace Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: channel-margin-workback.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sara Hayden <sara.hayden@terrafirm.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer draft + ask on listing and partner margin

Sara - quick note from channel: CloudBridge has a standard reseller margin policy that sets a practical floor of 18-22% depending on services. If we go with Jordan's Option B (invoice CloudBridge net of commission), two operational considerations:

1) AWS Marketplace metadata: private-offer flows where the invoiced party differs from the end-buyer still need the buyer field populated for reporting. We must ensure TerraFirm remains the listed buyer in the offer metadata to avoid usage attribution issues.

2) Tax & nexus: invoicing CloudBridge changes where tax is remitted. Irene - can you confirm whether Redwood can issue net invoices to CloudBridge without triggering US state nexus or VAT/GST complications? Laura - flag on revenue recognition: net invoicing can impact our gross vs net treatment for reseller commission - will need a short memo.

Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: invoice-routing-diagram.png (annotated)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sara Hayden <sara.hayden@terrafirm.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer draft + ask on listing and partner margin

Jordan / Ben / Sara - quick compliance & tax readout after a 30-min with finance ops:

- Tax: invoicing CloudBridge (as reseller) is feasible but requires us to collect CloudBridge's reseller certificate and to confirm their tax registration across states where TerraFirm consumes. If CloudBridge cannot provide certificates for all consumed nexus states, Redwood may be liable for sales tax in some jurisdictions.

- Revenue recognition: Laura is looped; high-level: net invoicing can be treated as agent vs principal depending on contract language and our commission terms. We need legal to confirm language in the PO that Redwood acts as the software vendor and CloudBridge as reseller. If we take Option A (increase discount), revenue recognition is cleaner for Redwood as principal.

- Operational: AWS private-offer listing must include the end-buyer (TerraFirm) as the buyer for proper marketplace usage attribution. We can implement invoice routing without changing the buyer field but must add a mapping record in our billing system. This will take 2-3 business days to configure.

Next steps: if TerraFirm confirms Option B, CloudBridge must send reseller certificates and we will prepare a short amendment to the PO describing invoice routing and commission flow.

Irene
Finance Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hayden <sara.hayden@terrafirm.com>, CloudBridge Channel <partner@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Updated PO + recommended path (Option B preferred)

Sara / CloudBridge team - thanks for the dialogue. Short summary and attachments:

What we propose (recommended): Option B - Redwood invoices CloudBridge net of reseller commission; TerraFirm remains the buyer in the AWS private-offer metadata. This preserves list-price visibility while letting CloudBridge show the required margin.

Deliverables attached:
- TF-Azure-PO-draft.pdf (PO updated with an invoice-routing amendment, payment instructions and required reseller certificate clause)
- channel-margin-workback.xlsx (shows both Option A and B economics; Option B preserves our ASP reporting)
- invoice-routing-diagram.png (how invoices flow end-to-end)

Ask from CloudBridge: please provide reseller certificates and confirm acceptance of the invoice timing (Net 30 from Redwood to CloudBridge). From TerraFirm: please confirm that keeping TerraFirm as the listed buyer in AWS is acceptable for procurement. If both confirm, we'll route the PO to Legal/Finance for final sign-off and send a DocuSign link by Friday 6/6.

If procurement prefers Option A, we'll update the PO with the additional discount and circulate the revised DocuSign envelope.

Thanks all,
Jordan
Head of Marketplace Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: TF-Azure-PO-draft.pdf; channel-margin-workback.xlsx; invoice-routing-diagram.png
